column1: # Where each policy is attached. Read by scripts/deploy-policies.sh.
# Attachment is configuration, not a flag on a command line. Before this file
# existed, --attach applied every policy to one target, which is wrong the
# moment any policy belongs somewhere else — and one does. It also left the
# actual attachment topology undocumented, recoverable only by querying AWS.
# Design doc 15 anticipates per-partner and per-client SCPs ("a partner with
# specific contractual constraints gets them at OU level"), so targets will
# only get more varied.
# Targets:
#   root      the Organization root — applies to every account in every OU.
#             Note SCPs never apply to the management account, wherever
#             attached, so "every account" excludes it by definition.
#   sandbox   the Sandbox OU — baseline canary, guardrail harness target
#   members   the Members OU — every partner, client and tenant account.
#             Requires --confirm-production.
#   security  the Security OU — Log Archive, Audit, Forensics. These hold the
#             evidence everything else is judged against, so they get the same
#             control protection as tenants rather than less.
#   infra     the Infrastructure OU — Platform Tooling, Shared Services, Backup.
# Columns: <policy file>  <TAB>  <comma-separated targets>
00-deny-leave-and-close-account.json
# 01-03 are mid-swap (B-135). The originals exempt role/Platform* by
# pattern; the -v2 files exempt named principals only. Each is ONE policy
# object attached to several OUs, so editing the original in place would
# change Members, Security and Infrastructure in the same API call as
# Sandbox. The v2s are separate objects: proven on Sandbox first, then
# swapped onto each other OU in 15.4, attaching the v2 before detaching the
# original, never the other way round. With 10 SCPs allowed per OU the swap
# goes one policy at a time. deploy-policies.sh never detaches; the detach is
# a deliberate step of its own. Swapped: Sandbox 2026-09-30; Infrastructure and
# Security 2026-10-01 (15.4a); Members 2026-10-01 (15.4b). When every OU carries the v2s, the originals
# are retired and these lines go.
# The originals are attached NOWHERE since 2026-10-01 (15.4b) and kept, detached,
# as a one-call rollback until Arc8 is live. Then delete them and these lines.
# 01-protect-detective-controls.json
# 02-protect-data-protection.json
# 03-protect-platform-identity.json
01-protect-detective-controls-v2.json
02-protect-data-protection-v2.json
03-protect-platform-identity-v2.json
# 04 is sandbox-only until a tenant exists to negotiate it with. It is the
# only policy in this set that denies ordinary CREATION rather than
# tampering with a control, so it is the only one that can stop a
# developer working. Widening it to members is a conversation, not a
# deployment.
04-require-tags.json
# 05 is sandbox-only for the same reason as 04: it denies an action
# developers legitimately take. Widening it to members needs every
# tenant pipeline that creates a role to be passing the boundary first,
# which is a conversation and a migration rather than a deployment.
05-require-boundary.json
# 06 and 07 are sandbox-only for now. 06 especially: attached to
# members it denies every action in an unapproved region, including to
# a tenant pipeline that deploys somewhere nobody checked. That is a
# conversation before it is a deployment.
06-region-restriction.json
07-deny-bypass.json
# 08 is design 11 Layer 1's "platform-managed alarms and SSM associations",
# which 01-03 never carried (B-148). PowerUserAccess in dev could rewrite the
# response engine's code, disable the drift rule that recreates deleted
# alarms, or flip /platform/response/enabled off -- each one a monitoring
# control removed by somebody the platform is meant to be monitoring.
# Sandbox first, same as the v2 swap: the harness proves it there, then
# members is added here and deployed with --confirm-production. Members then
# carries nine of its ten SCPs (eight platform plus FullAWSAccess), so the
# next control after this one extends an existing policy rather than adding.
08-protect-platform-monitoring.json
# The first RCP. design 11 names cross-account trust as a bypass, and no
# SCP condition key can see a trust policy's Principal -- an RCP
# evaluates on the RESOURCE side and denies the assume itself. D-003.
00-no-external-principals.json
